newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban deny any extra-territorial intentions.
newsitem.headline: Taleban deny any extra-territorial intentions.

text.p: The purist Islamic Taleban movement said in a statement on Sunday it had no intention of spreading its values beyond the borders of Afghanistan.
"Steps within the framework of the demands of the Afghan people towards the enforcement of Islamic Sharia in the country have been taken and the results of these steps look promising.

"However, the Islamic State of Afghanistan neither had, nor has, any intention of spreading these values outside its geographical borders." the statement, released by the Foreign Ministry on Sunday afternoon, said.

It was issued in response to a meeting of the foreign ministers of four Central Asian republics -- Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan -- and the Russian first deputy foreign minister in the Tajik captial of Dushanbe on Saturday.

In a joint communique released after the meeting, the ministers expressed concern at the continuation of armed hostilities in Afghanistan and stated their readiness for "close joint action" in protecting their common borders, although what form this action would take was not made clear in the communique.

The Central Asian states share much of their southern borders with Afghanistan. Most of the Afghan side of the border is at present held by an opposition alliance which the Taleban have vowed to dislodge.
Turkmenistan, the only Central Asian state that shares a border with Taleban-held Afghanistan, was not represented at the Dushanbe meeting.
"Turkmenistan, based on its realistic policies, did not take part in the meeting." the Taleban statement said.

The four Central Asian states, most of which are led by former communist party bosses, are nervous that the Taleban will try to export their puritanical vision of Islam, further undermining Central Asia's fragile stability.
The Central Asinns are also nervous that a Taleban victory in northern Afghanstan would push large numbers of refugees over the border into their territory.
The Taleban statement says that Russia is exaggerating the threat posed by the Taleban to maintain its military presence in Central Asia.

"The creation of unwarranted fear that a Taleban advance into the north of the country would be damaging to he interests of the Central Asian states is merely face-saving by Moscow, which does not wish to see the development of independence among the Central Asian states.
"The Central Asian states should be aware of Moscow's policies, which aim to maintain the permanent military presence of the Russian Federation in the region." the statement said.
The Taleban statement went on to reiterate the Taleban's committment to non-interference in the affairs of other countries.

"The Islamic State of Afghanistan is committed to international laws regarding the right to sovereignty and national independence and supports the principle of non- interference in the affairs of other countries." it said.
It added that Afghanistan, after years of war, was in no position to destabilise other countries.

"Even with a superficial look at the situation in Afghanistan, it is understandable that the economic, military, technical, and cultural potential of the country has been exhausted by the continuing hostilities.
"Afghanistan is in no position to create problems or harass powerful countries." it added.
